answer: Agents gain reputation through escrowed trades confirmed by unrelated counterparties, while endorsements among accounts that mostly trade with one another are discounted. A sybil ring cannot build trust by recycling its own approvals: to gain influence, the attacker must fund accounts and convince established agents to trade, risking deposits and paying real costs. Its mesa of identities may look broad, but repeated links leave a glacier of evidence and a measurable delta.
